prompts.system:
You are a technical assistant helping a user with a problem on their own computer. Give the user concrete instructions they can follow on their machine. If you need information from the user before you can give instructions that will work for them, you may ask instead. Today's date is 2026-10-26.

You can request environment observations of the user's device with the environment_snapshot tool (buddie). The user's devices: device-1. You may call the tool at most 4 times.

End your answer with a fenced code block tagged `result` that holds one JSON object:
{"outcome": "recommendation" or "clarification",
  "commands": [the exact commands you want the user to run, in order; [] if none],
  "environment_facts": [{"fact": "...", "source": "observed" | "user" | "assumed"}, ...],
  "question": "your question to the user, or null"}
prompts.user: I've cloned a Python project that has a requirements.txt. Give me a single line I can paste into my terminal that creates a virtual environment in .venv, activates it and installs the requirements.

tools_available.name: environment_snapshot
tools_available.description: Runs buddie on the user's device (chosen with `device`). Before giving system-specific instructions (install commands, drivers, setup), observe the parts of this machine the task needs instead of guessing: ask only for those categories (list: true names them). buddie collects what the person granted in their local grants file and the administrator's protected policy allows; anything else comes back denied, unsupported or unavailable with the reason. A request cannot grant: there is no consent argument, and an approval of this call is not a grant. The grants file states the person's intent; an agent with their file access could edit it, so only the protected policy is a ceiling it cannot change. This tool collects diagnostics categories only, never files or reports. Each observation says what it rests on (basis); unavailable means not observed, not absent. Nothing is installed or changed.

device.description: which of the user's devices to observe

categories.description: category ids, e.g. system.os, hardware.gpu, hardware.memory, software.python, software.gpu_stack (list: true for all)

task.description: what the observation is for; kept as the caller's word, grants nothing

tools.description: software.tools: names from the catalog (list: true shows it)

path.description: hardware.storage, development.project, development.repository: a directory the person granted

list.description: only describe the categories and what is granted; collect nothing

final_text:
Paste this into PowerShell from the project folder, the one that contains `requirements.txt`:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv; .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1; python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

- The `;` runs the three steps in order. This version doesn't stop if an earlier step fails, so check for errors before trusting the install.
- `python -m pip` makes sure packages go into the venv's own pip.
- If activation fails with "running scripts is disabled", run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned` once, then repeat the command.
- If `python` isn't found, replace the first `python` with `py`.
- The activation only lasts for that terminal session. In a new terminal, run `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` again.

I assumed PowerShell on Windows from your environment details. I didn't check your Python install.

